LUMEN DEMONSTRATOR USER EVALUATION REPORT V1.0

1. Executive summary

The LUMEN demonstrator evaluation involved twelve participants: six archive professionals, four researchers, and two postgraduate students. Sessions took place from 8 to 19 June 2026 in Spanish and English.

Every participant completed seven tasks concerning search, approximate dates, historical people, place names, relations, language switching, and rights. Participants then completed a questionnaire and took part in a short interview.

The overall success rate was 84%. Median task time was 2 minutes 46 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 97% of journeys. Understanding of approximate dates reached 88%, while interpretation of creator, author, and producer roles reached 72%.

2. Scope

Evaluation uses the candidate demonstrator, second ingestion, and authorized objects. It does not include editing, bulk download, or search across every Regional Archive collection. Results apply to the versions recorded in the manifest.

3. Method

The starting language was alternated. Tasks had verifiable answers and used different objects to reduce learning. Observers recorded actions, time, assistance, and comments but did not retain complete text from personal searches.

Quantitative results were complemented by journey and interview analysis. Problems were classified as data, terminology, interface, rights, performance, or task. Wording difficulty was not automatically attributed to the system.

Evaluation section 1

Task 1 was to locate a photograph using a topic and period. The objective was to use search and filters without knowing the identifier. Complete success, partial success, failure, time, actions, assistance, path, and comments were recorded. The reviewer compared the outcome with the source and distinguished a data, terminology, interface, or task error. Results were analyzed by profile and language. An ambiguous task was reviewed before being used for a conclusion.
